title: The SRC registry departs from its own specification on both member expertise and verified addresses
content:
Two requirements and the data that is supposed to satisfy them do not match.

A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.5.1 states that "SRC members shall be domain experts across security, risk/economics, and operations," and .5.2 fixes the seat count at three. A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.11 specifies that the registry records "name or alias, domain expertise, **verified governance address**, start date, term status, and standing."

The live registry at A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.11.1.0.6.1 lists Blockworks Advisory, L2 Beat and Aragon — all seated 2025-10-03, all Active, and all with `Domain Expertise: Risk` and `Verified Governance Address: N/A`.

With three seats and three risk specialists, the mandated coverage of security and operations is unfilled. Whether "across" means each member is broad or the body collectively spans the three domains, neither reading is satisfied by three entries reading "Risk" — which matters because the Scope of Review at .4.2 explicitly includes "security vulnerabilities and operational attack surface" as reviewable categories.

The blank addresses are the smaller but cleaner discrepancy: a field the Artifact requires, present in the schema and empty in every row. It also means SRC determinations are not cryptographically attributable the way Delegate votes are, despite the SRC wielding a stronger power.

Both gaps are, notably, visible *because* the Artifact specifies the fields and publishes the data in the same document. The structure makes its own shortfalls auditable — which is the argument for this style of governance artifact even when the shortfalls are real.
description: The Artifact requires expertise across security, risk/economics and operations plus a verified governance address, yet all three seated members list Risk only and address N/A.
